old_title: Yorkshire v Somerset, Sussex v Notts and more: County Championship cricket, day two - live
new_title: Points deduction puts Leicestershire on brink as Warwickshire go top: County Championship cricket, day two - as it happened
old_text:
In a quiet corner of the Championship, at Bristol, Middlesex added only another couple of runs this morning, and in reply Gloucestershire are 63 for one. Joe Phillips an early wicket to Morgan. Despite the organisational carnage, I do think Middlesex are a team with potential. Definite promotion candidates next year.
Biff! Four smacked through the offside and that's the Pretorius fifty, off 59 balls. He raises his bat to the dressing room who roar encouragement. More! More! The deficit 48. What a timely highest-score of the season.
Back to Division Two where Kent, showing a Div One fighting spirit, shimmied a first-innings lead of 53. And Lancs, I'm afraid, have already lost Jennings, caught in slow motion with basket hands by Crawley at slip for a two-ball duck off Khaled. Lancs 8 for one.
The third Somerset fifty has come up in just 51 balls, as Overton sticks his huge front pad forward and prods Kuldeep away. The Leeds sun is still turning the turf a luminous green. The deficit 60.
The BBC's Kevin Howells walks past with a coffee, "it's all very well people getting excited about next week," he says, "it's all being played out in front of our eyes right now."
Overton and Pretorius meanwhile have reduced the deficit to 75.
And no century for Zak Crawley, who by all accounts has played outstandingly for his 84. This was Matt Milnes last night: "the way Zak batted was incredible, really. I thought, on that pitch and in the situation, that was worth 160 rather than 60 or whatever it is. So, yeah, it was a serious knock."
Kent, now 200-9, have a gold-dust lead of 40 over Lancs (28 of them extras).
No! No century for the other Ollie Robinson, who must be satisfied with his highest score of a (relatively) lean year. Last man out for 97. Good luck Worcestershire for the coming onslaught.
Is this the morning that secured the title for Warwickshire? We don't know. We can't know. But what we do know that their slim 17 runs lead overnight, nine wickets down, has since swelled to 57 before finally being bowled out for 191 by Essex. Sam Hain went from 58 not out to 88 not out, OHD gave it the barn door for 28 balls and then edged the 29th to slip. Tall Paul Walter snaffling the catch, having given OHD a life - and his only runs of the innings - with an earlier drop.
Pretorius is being attended to after he gets hit on the hand from a nasty Ben Cliff ball. Cliff, 23 and with a few England U19 appearances under his belt, has his best bowling by a long way in this innings: six for 37. Somerset 87 for eight.
Look away, and Cliff has another, a searing ball which spits and Leach gets an edge through to Bairstow. Somerset 86 for eight and floundering after a pretty catastrophic first 25 minutes.
Non rhythmic applause as Ben Cliff approaches his hat-trick, but no cigar this time.
But some good news for Somerset and Warwicks, Notts have missed out on a batting point at Hove by ten runs, the hard-grafting Hutton last man out for 60.
And next ball, the dream gets a little smaller. Gregory takes off his gloves and with tiny steps drifts away, lbw and given out with a flourish. Five wickets for Cliff who is on a hat-trick. Somerset 74 for seven.
A huge Headingley roar as James Rew edges behind to Jonny Bairstow, a fourth wicket for young Cliff. Craig Overton cowboys down the pitch to talk tactics with the incoming Lewis Gregory. Somerset 74 for six.
The skies over God's Own County are dazzling, though there's a fair wind. I've been pointed towards these comments by Somerset's bowling coach Steve Kirby about the Headingley pitch.
"It's not the best surface. If I'm completely honest, I thought the pitch was doing considerably more than when we got done against Durham (July 25, Taunton, four-point penalty). I'm bit a disappointed with that and thought it would be a lot, lot better."
"There's enough going on without it being the other end of crazy"
Some thoughtful chat about pitches in the Reporters' Network quotes last night:
Glamorgan's Zain ul Hassan, who took four for 26 in Surrey's 115 all out at The Oval:
"There have been a lot of result pitches around in these final weeks of the season and that's I think because there are quite a lot of teams either going for the Championship, trying to avoid relegation or get promoted.
"More pitches have been greener and it has been really hard for batting around the country."
And Hampshire's Scott Currie at Grace Road:
"The pitch is doing a bit but when you're at the bottom of the league, I think teams earn the right at home to do what they like with the pitches. As bowlers, we're not going to complain - I had a season on loan here and I wish the pitches had done as much then.
"We never had a wicket with shaved ends while I was here but credit to Alfonso Thomas, Claude Henderson and the ground staff here for trying to produce wickets that are doing a bit. Some balls have gone up, some have gone down, but no one's been hit. There's enough going on without it being the other end of crazy."
A brow-mopping 123 wickets fell on the first day of the penultimate round of matches as the season hurtled towards the autumn trapdoor. It was difficult to know what to make of it, though title-hunting Somerset might repent at leisure the last half of the evening session at Headingley, which they finished on 68 for five. Jonny Bairstow's busy 79 had hauled Yorkshire to 212, though he was dropped twice. Much rests on the oaken shoulders of Craig Overton.
With clouds building and floodlights on, Nottinghamshire crawled towards a precious batting point at Hove against Sussex's parsimonious bowlers, something that seemed risible until a ninth-wicket stand of 74 between Brett Hutton and Tom Giles. Hutton's two-and-a-half-hour 59 was the highest score of the innings.
A career-best six for 26 by Ethan Bamber helped keep Essex down as Warwickshire drove for points at Chelmsford. Essex were whistled out for 134, though that was riches from the ashes of 33 for seven, thanks largely to an unbeaten 61 from the on-loan wicketkeeper George Bell, who has jumped out of the Old Trafford frying pan to find his boots burning again. But Warwickshire wouldn't have it all their own way as they too collapsed, 151 for nine at stumps, a slender lead of just 17 runs.
Zak Crawley curated the only half-century at Canterbury to bring Kent in touching distance of Lancashire's 161.
There was a cascade of 20 wickets at the Oval, where neither Glamorgan nor Surrey could reach the heady heights of 140. Matt Fisher limped out of the game with a groin injury.
Ian Holland's career-best six for 38 dismissed Hampshire for 214 in the Division One battle for the wooden spoon. Ben Brown's unbeaten 80 saved his side too many blushes. Leicestershire, who are still waiting for the Cricket Regulator to rule on their pitch, shuffled to 148 for seven, thanks to fifty from Hamza Shaikh.
At Chester-le-Street the runs ran freely as India's Mayank Agarwal blazed Worcestershire's bowlers around the ground with a dazzling 177. For once, Ben Stokes had to play second fiddle, though his thunderbolt 50 off 40 balls delighted the faithful who had come to wallow in autumn sunshine and the warmth of promotion. Durham were cruising to a full set of batting points before the setting sun spoiled their fun.
Hundreds for Derbyshire's Ben Aitchison and Wayne Madsen stayed Northamptonshire's promotion push.
Good morning! It's grey travelling across the Pennines, the cloud low, leaves rusty, train, endpoint Scarborough, empty. A bowling alley day yesterday, wickets for fun, special shoes or not, and runs a desperate struggle except for Wayne Madsen, Ben Aitchison and the magnificent Mayank Agarwal. Do join us for more chaos from 10.30 as day two unfolds.
new_text:
Points deduction puts Leicestershire on brink as Warwickshire go top: County Championship cricket, day two - as it happened
It was advantage Warwickshire at the top but the most significant action came off the pitch, with Leicestershire all but relegated after a points deduction
Roundup: Warwickshire win but points deduction puts Leicestershire on brink
It was advantage Warwickshire at the top but perhaps the most significant action of the day came off the pitch and at the bottom, with Leicestershire all but relegated after a points deduction.
The Cricket Regulator had charged Leicestershire after the Grace Road pitch was rated as poor for last month's win against Glamorgan. The cricket discipline panel has upheld the charge, leading to the deduction of the 19 points picked up for the victory plus eight more as a penalty. A Leicestershire statement said "the club is reviewing its position and considering all available options", but the deduction left them bottom of the table, 38 points adrift of the last safe spot. With Hampshire 225 ahead with seven wickets standing, Leicestershire's hopes in what is now a must-win match are slim.
Warwickshire flourish a 19-point hand on the table and wait after a second two-day victory in succession. Essex, further weakened by overnight substitutions to Shane Snater and Tom Westley, gave them the upper hand by conceding another 40 runs for the last wicket, thanks largely to an unbeaten 88 from Sam Hain. The Indian spinner Manav Suthar, with five for 75, and Chris Woakes, with three for 33, were too hot for Essex and Warwickshire easily knocked off the 133 needed.
The morning bell at Chelmsford was rung by the BBC's Dick Davies, retiring after 31 years covering Essex cricket. Up at Headingley, Craig Overton continued his one-man attempt to haul Somerset over the line. His 64 not out, full of humpty and grace, rescued his team from the doldrums of 86 for eight, in companionship with Migael Pretorius, who found his long-lost batting form with a free-flowing 58.
Overton was last man out to Ben Cliff's, whose astonishing eight for 76 were the best bowling figures for a Yorkshireman at Headingley since Graham Stevenson's eight for 57 in 1980. He led Yorkshire off grinning, applauding teammates behind.
Overton soon spoiled their fun, nobbling Will Luxton's middle stump with his second ball, and removing Adam Lyth a couple of overs later. Jonny Bairstow came and went to a Nureyev catch at cover by Archie Vaughan but George Hill and Dom Bess stopped the rot with an unbroken seventh-wicket stand of 74 as spectators in the East Stand enjoyed some afternoon sun to stretch Yorkshire's lead to 139.
At Hove, Nottinghamshire were held up by an obdurate Sussex, who picked up the only Division One batting point of the round thanks to half centuries for Tom Clark, Charlie Tear and Tom Price.
Kent need 56 to beat Lancashire and get their promotion points on the board. Zak Crawley (84) and Matt Milnes (40 not out) ushered Kent to a first-innings lead of 53, before Milnes had a go with the ball and helped chisel Lancashire out for 192. Sam Northeast and Tawanda Muyeye took Kent towards a good night's sleep.
Asa Tribe's first hundred of the season, on a wicket where 20 wickets had fallen the day before, eased Glamorgan's relegation nerves, even before the Leicestershire news.
It's dark outside the Headingley press box, the white covers just visible through the gloom. Well played Warwickshire, what a late-season run. We'll be here tomorrow to see if Somerset can catch them, and more. Thanks for your company, have a lovely evening.
Stumps at Headingley too, with Hill and Bess threatening to take this Somerset total into the worrying category for Somerset. Yorks 128 for six, lead by 139. Time for me to write up for the paper.
A huge farewell to Dick who is about to finish commentating on BBC Essex after 31 years. A gentle, knowledgable presence. Have a wonderful retirement .
At Grace Road Nick Gubbins is undefeated on 124 at stumps. Hampshire's best day for a long time, and they can sleep on a lead of 225, with seven wickets in hand.
Warwickshire are going to win in two days again, to chalk those points on the slate. They've lost Yates, for 33, but only need 46 to sends Essex's season sliding closer to the trap door.
Applause round Headingley as the Yorkshire lead reaches three figures. And now we have Jack Leach.
Three wickets each for Khaled, Milnes and Dudgeon at Canterbury in Lancs' 192 all out. Harris (48) and Jones (54) propped the innings up. With promotion dangling, can Kent buckle through?
A first hundred of a tricky season for Nick Gubbins! Grace Road has lost its daemons and Hampshire lead Leicestershire by 200, eight wickets in hand.
And a nice stat from the ACS: Hants teammate Aneurin Donald is the first person with his forename to play any format of international cricket (the most famous achievement by anyone of that name is founding the UK's National Health Service).
They're sunbathing in the East Stand as young colt George Hill keeps Yorkshire roses in bloom. Kevin Howells drops another bon mots as he sips on his press box coffee "if Somerset do go on to win the Championship it will be impossible to overstate the role of Craig Overton." There he stands at second slip, arms crossed, boots two metres apart.
"Hello Tanya. Sweating over Bears prospects here in Mozambique, but Somerset seem indomitable. I saw just a day's County cricket this year, at Trent Bridge in April. Big score from Warks, but unwise to enforce follow on and knacker your bowlers. Nottingham people may be the most friendly in England. I read Ashes hype, already, but world champions first! I will be on a grassy bank in Pretoria (before Christmas this year) and Joburg." I'm very envious! An intriguing series.
Khaled and Dudgeon are chipping away at Lancashire who are 163-7. A negligible but not improper lead of 110 with Jimmy, Stanley and Balderson waiting to bowl.
Gregory bends the knee and nods his head, like a joyful mountain goat. Abell gobbles up again at second slip as Whiteman is sent on his way for a dutiful 35. Yorks 54 for six.
Somerset think Gregory has two in two but the umpire says no.
Archie Vaughan takes a stupendous leaping catch in the covers to send YJB on his way, then runs about with a cap in his hand like a 1950's schoolboy as he is mobbed by his teammates. Yorkshire 45 for five. Gregory the bowler.
Essex have folded for 189. Five for Suthan, three for Woakes. Can Essex, without Shane Snater, without Jamie Porter, without Simon Harmer do anything to stop the bears. Simon Cook is partnered by 17 year old Jack Auld.
Somerset swarm with a skip and a hop as Revis finally falls for a dogged, 41-ball two. He nibbles at Ball and Abell does the rest. Yorks 40 for four. A bow legged figure strides onto the grass.
According to Richard Gibson's reports in the Daily Mail, there will be four Championship fixtures next June and July to give England's Ashes players more access to red-ball practice around the series. It compares with two matches in June this year.
There are three Someset slips to Ball. All of them wearing cream cable knit sweaters. Revis has a sudden swish and miss. Around the stands are clusters of fans in quiet absorption. Yorkshire 31 for three.
After all the pre-season hype, a Championship century at last for Tribe, and it might just secure first-division cricket for Glamorgan next year. Glamorgan 240 for three.
I meant to post this round preview from Gary Naylor, yesterday. The umpires are walking out at Headingley, and the groundstaff immediately start to haul in the sheets.
Right - let's trot around the grounds whille they take an early tea at Headingley, now in bright sunshine.
Warwickshire look like being first over the finishing line, after reducing Essex to 139 for five in their second innings, a lead of just 82.
Hampshire are fighting back at Grace Road after Leicestershire picked up a first-innings lead of 30. A fifty for Nick Gubbins leading the way in 113-1.
Kiran Carlson has just been out for 57 at The Oval but Tribe still there on 88. Glamorgan 210-3, lead Surrey by 227.
Notts have winkled out Tom Clark for 89, but Sussex are staying strong at 170-3, trail Notts by 68.
Apropros of nothing, I read a lovely piece on the late great Rob Steen this morning, by Huw Richards in the latest Nightwatchman. Suddenly they're coming off at Headingley for rain - Yorkshire 26 for three. Quite a lot of rain actually. Leeds suddenly disappearing into the gloom.
Stephen Moss (that one) writes in to say that he later found out, and was sad to miss, that a fox appeared at The Oval yesterday and briefly stopped play. It's a different gravy in south London today, where Glamorgan have eased to 189-2 - Tribe 82 not out, Carlson 43 not out. The lead over Surrey, 206.
Nicholls makes no mistake at first slip as Adam Lyth mis-dabs. Overton, of course. Hands on hips, he is already walking back to his mark. Yorkshire five for two.
The clouds were gathering around Headingley at lunch and Somerset were out in the middle, stretching, bowling, catching.
Thanks to Chris Waters of the Yorkshire Post for the lowdown on Ben Cliff. His figures were the best for a Yorkshireman since Craig White's 8-55 at Glos in 1998, and the best at Headingley since Graham Stevenson's 8-57 v Northants in 1980.
